# Guarded stock update after a successful charge

> After Stripe has charged the card, one guarded SQL `UPDATE` takes the bought quantity out of the product's stock, and only if enough stock is still there.

_Part of [Optimistic stock deduction](optimistic-stock-deduction.md)_

This step lives inside the `Finalize Transaction` block of `PaymentService.executePayment`. It runs only when Stripe says the charge `succeeded` and the request has a `productId`. Before charging, the service did a cheap stock look-up. That look-up can be wrong if another buyer grabs the stock in between, so this update is the real guard. See [Optimistic stock deduction](optimistic-stock-deduction.md) for the full idea. The Stock-decrement UPDATE with a quantity guard subtracts the quantity, adds 1 to `version`, and matches the row only when `quantity >= :quantity`. It runs in the same database transaction as the payment status update. The code then reads Row count of the stock update: the number of rows the update changed. If the row count is 0, stock ran out after the card was charged. The code returns early with a Early return that asks for a refund. The payment stays `PENDING`, and no ledger entry or success message is written. The caller then refunds Stripe outside the transaction and marks the payment `REFUNDED`. See [Refund when stock runs out after charging](refund-saga.md). If the row count is 1, the code carries on to mark the payment `COMPLETED` and post the ledger journal.

**Look at:** [`PaymentService.executePayment` in payment.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/application/payment.service.ts#L65)

## Pieces

- Stock-decrement UPDATE with a quantity guard: An `UPDATE "Product"` that lowers `quantity`, raises `version`, and matches only when enough stock is left, returning the row `id`.
- Row count of the stock update: `rowCount` is read from the query result, defaulting to 0, and tells whether the guarded update changed a row.
- Early return that asks for a refund: When the row count is 0, the transaction returns the payment, `needsRefund: true` and the Stripe payment intent id, so the caller can refund.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Product` | Its `quantity` is decreased and its `version` increased, but only if `quantity >= :quantity`. |
| external | `Stripe` | The charge has already succeeded before this step. If the stock update fails, the payment intent is refunded afterwards. |

## Also relies on

- [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md): This step is part of the finalize phase of `PaymentService.executePayment`, which runs after the Stripe charge.

## Watch out

- The update runs after the card is charged, so losing the race means a refund, not a rejected order.
- A row count of 0 does not throw an error. The code returns early with `needsRefund`, and the refund happens later.
- On the refund path the payment stays `PENDING` inside the transaction. It becomes `REFUNDED` only in a later transaction, after Stripe has refunded.
- The stock look-up before charging gives no guarantee. Only this guarded `UPDATE` stops overselling.
